title: Apply Operations to an Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed array of non-negative integers, apply n-1 operations where each operation multiplies the i-th element by 2 if it equals the (i+1)-th element, and sets the (i+1)-th element to 0.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array of non-negative integers, apply n-1 operations where each operation multiplies the i-th element by 2 if it equals the (i+1)-th element, and sets the (i+1)-th element to 0. After all operations, shift all zeros to the end. Return the modified array.
constraints: Scan indexes left to right once.
When adjacent values are equal, double the left value and replace the right value with zero.
After the scan, move all zeroes to the end while preserving nonzero order.
hints: Simulate the adjacent operations before moving any zeroes.
At each index, compare the current value with the next value, because earlier operations may have changed it.
After one left-to-right pass, collect nonzero values and append enough zeroes to restore the length.
The simulation follows the required order exactly, and stable compaction preserves the mandated nonzero order.
editorial: The simulation follows the required order exactly, and stable compaction preserves the mandated nonzero order.

tests.explanation: The two pairs combine during the scan, then compaction gives [1,4,2,0,0,0].
No equal adjacent operation changes the values, and compaction gives [1,0].
